original_question: Assume the P-ideal dichotomy, namely that for every P-ideal I of countable subsets of some index set S either there is an uncountable T subset of S whose countable subsets all belong to I, or S can be decomposed into countably many pieces with no infinite subset in I. Under that assumption, are the following equivalent: (1) every non-separable Banach space has an uncountable biorthogonal system, and (2) b = aleph_2?

refined_question: Assume the P-ideal dichotomy (PID): for every P-ideal I of countable subsets of a set S (i.e. for every sequence (A_n) in I there is A in I such that A_n \ A is finite for all n), either there is an uncountable T ⊆ S such that every countable subset of T belongs to I, or S can be partitioned into countably many pieces having no infinite subset in I. Under PID, are the following equivalent? (1) Every non-separable Banach space X has an uncountable biorthogonal system, i.e. there exist an uncountable set Γ and a family {(xγ, xγ*)}_{γ∈Γ} ⊆ X × X* such that xγ*(xδ) = δγδ for all γ, δ ∈ Γ. (2) The bounding number 𝔟 equals ℵ2, where 𝔟 is the least cardinality of an unbounded family in (ω^ω, ≤*), with f ≤* g meaning f(n) ≤ g(n) for all sufficiently large n.
justification: The draft is targeting the paper’s Problem 17 exactly, not a neighboring result. Section 11 develops the surrounding context by first discussing quotients with long Schauder bases (Problem 16), then introducing PID, then stating Theorem 17 and Corollary 18, and finally posing Problem 17 in the precise form: whether, assuming PID, the statement that every non-separable Banach space has an uncountable biorthogonal system is equivalent to 𝔟 = ℵ2. The only substantive omissions in the draft are the paper’s earlier definition of 𝔟 and an explicit definition of 'uncountable biorthogonal system,' both of which are needed to make the question fully stand-alone and paper-faithful.
